Committee: State Government
Sponsor: Clarke
Analyst: John Friedenreich
Date: 02/17/2021
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 179 as introduced will allow the Director of the State Port Authority to appoint and fix the salaries of two additional non-merit system executive level employees who could replace current merit system executive level employees who retire or otherwise leave the employment of the port authority. This could increase the Port Authority's obligations by an unknown amount that would be dependent upon the salaries established for the two non-merit executive level employees and whether they are additional employees or replacement for existing employees, as well as the salaries of the merit system employee being replaced, if applicable. The average salary of the nine executive level employees authorized prior to this bill is approximately $157,000.
Chris Pringle, Chair
State Government

Committee: Governmental Affairs
Sponsor: Ingram
Analyst: Vee Mosely
Date: 03/04/2021
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 165 as passed the House of Representatives could reduce receipts to the State General Fund and the Secretary of State Entity Fund by $17.50 and $7.50, respectively, for each certificate of existence fee the Secretary of State elects to waive.
According to Secretary of State, the average annual distributions from these fees are estimated to be $265,000 to the State General Fund and $114,000 to the Secretary of State Entity Fund.
Jimmy Holley, Chairperson
Governmental Affairs
